unobservedLedgerEntries.label: L-03
unobservedLedgerEntries.origin: still-open (not re-observed as a candidate; carried, not closed)
reasoning: L-03 has two clauses. (a) The global Pauser loop reverts on pre-paused registrants. (b) Phase 8 asserts registration, not a working breaker.

Clause (a) is gone only because the owner changed on-chain state (unregistered the paused contracts; test_B pause() SUCCEEDS 27/27). The script did not change to cause this. The trigger can come back any time a registered contract is paused by another path, and the script would not notice.

Clause (b) is unchanged at 884ccf8. Phase 8 (CutoverStableStakerV2Mainnet.s.sol ~L633-639) still has only pauser()/isRegistered()/paused() requires and no simulated `Pauser.pause()`. The script that hands V2 and Antimatter their only pause authority still never proves the breaker works.

Under Law 1, clearing the trigger through external state is not a verified fix. The emergency-breaker verification gap is the part that protects against exploits. SSV2C32-01 also shows the global pause reverting mid-run on the current code, which confirms the breaker's health is not guaranteed by construction.

Recommend finding-manager narrow the note (the trigger is currently cleared on-chain; clause (b) is live) and keep function/rootCauseClass unchanged. If the owner accepts the clause (b) gap as a residual risk, that is a human wont-fix/acknowledged decision, not `fixed`. Propose `fixed` only once Phase 8 (or preview) runs a simulated `Pauser.pause()` against the post-finalize registry.
